recentItems.title: Labour Party conference: can ‘Burnham bounce’ survive economic reality?
recentItems.description:
Labour delegates in Liverpool are talking about hope again, but can the mood reach the wider public?

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

The UK under Prime Minister Andy Burnham has reset its position on Israel, Gaza and the West Bank, according to Labour’s foreign secretary. In Liverpool, Ed Miliband admitted at the Labour Party conference that Sir Keir Starmer’s government was wrong.

But ahead of Burnham’s appearance at the conference on Tuesday, members of his cabinet have struggled to be quite as clear about what they got wrong and what they will change.

It is hard to see, for example, what in the chancellor's speech couldn't have been said by his predecessor, as he promised to stick to the fiscal rules, reindustrialise Britain and reform welfare. 

Experts disagree how big and how significant the "Burnham bounce" in the polls has been, but there's no denying that there has been a significant bounce in the spirits and strides of delegates at the conference. 

So if party activists are learning to "hope again" as the slogan plastered around Liverpool says, can they transfer that sentiment around the country?

recentItems.title: What is the Orange Order, and why has their parade been stopped?
recentItems.description:
Thousands of protesters, including Northern Ireland First Minister Michelle O’Neill and Sinn Féin 

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

president Mary Lou McDonald, blocked the Garvaghy Road in Portadown to prevent a Loyalist Orange Order parade from passing.

The parade had been given permission to use the route for the first time in almost 30 years, but police stopped the marchers from reaching the road.

The Orange Order says the road is part of its traditional route, while many Catholic, Nationalist residents oppose the parade passing through their community.

The dispute dates back to the Troubles, when clashes over the Drumcree parade led to serious violence.

recentItems.title: Fairford suspects bailed: why were five British men questioned and released?
recentItems.description:
The five men arrested near RAF Fairford on suspicion of explosives and terror offences have been released on police bail as Iran condemned what it called unfounded, malicious speculation.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Events at RAF Fairford, the Gloucestershire airbase used by the US military, have raised questions about national security during Labour’s conference in Liverpool.

So was it an Iranian backed plot? The government in Tehran has denied that it was.

What we do know is that five young British men, all Londoners in their early twenties, have now been bailed.

recentItems.title: Mariana Mazzucato: ‘We need SMARTER government, not less government’
recentItems.description:
Can John Healey deliver the growth Britain desperately needs?

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

At Labour’s conference in Liverpool, the Chancellor promised a new age of industrialisation, more opportunities for young people and an era of political hope. But with the government under pressure to control spending, what does that mean for welfare, public investment and the economy?
In this episode of The Fourcast, Krishnan Guru-Murthy speaks to economist Mariana Mazzucato and Times columnist Fraser Nelson. They debate how Britain can grow its economy, whether welfare reform can get more people into work, and whether the government should cut taxes and regulation or invest more heavily in public services and infrastructure.
